text:
Situation: Sterile water has been on FDA's shortage list since 2021-11-23 and remains current as of 2026-10-21, a span of 59 months. Current inventory across Corvale sites ranges from 2.4 to 19.6 days of supply, with the lowest coverage at Corvale East for 10 mL single-dose vials (2.4 days) and 5 mL single-dose vials (2.7 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2021-11-23. An inspection of Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited ended 2019-09-06 and was classified OAI, with the classification letter dated 2020-05-25 (547 days before the shortage posting). FDA issued a Warning Letter to Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited on 2020-03-25 (608 days before posting). FDA issued a Warning Letter to Nephron SC, LLC on 2020-09-22 (427 days before posting). FDA's OAI classification letter to Hospira, Inc. is dated 2020-04-22 (580 days before posting).

Our position: Supply is critically low at multiple sites. The rule-identified best option is American Regent, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and whose plant last received a VAI classification on 2024-04-24. Two alternate manufacturers (Hospira, Inc. and Nephron Pharmaceuticals Corporation) have prior pharmacist approval for NDC substitution with no clinical change.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place orders with American Regent, Inc. as primary source; requires buyer approval.
2. Buyer to qualify Novo Nordisk and Sandoz Inc. as secondary sources; requires buyer approval.
3. Pharmacist to activate NDC substitution to Hospira, Inc. product per Riley Brooks, PharmD approval dated 2026-05-18; requires pharmacist approval.
4. Pharmacist to activate NDC substitution to Nephron Pharmaceuticals Corporation product per Jordan Hale, PharmD approval dated 2026-07-31; requires pharmacist approval.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or therapeutic alternatives; those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.
